question.problem:
Find $\text{E}[{X}^{3}-2X],$ given that the continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function

$$
f(x)=\frac{{x}^{2}}{9},\,0\le x\le 3.
$$
question.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ and a function $r(x),$ the rule of the lazy statistician states that 

$$
\text{E}[r(X)]={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }r(x)f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, we have 

$$
r(x)={x}^{3}-2x.
$$

 

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{3}-2X] & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }r(x)f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}({x}^{3}-2x)\cdot \frac{{x}^{2}}{9}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}(\frac{{x}^{5}}{9}-\frac{2{x}^{3}}{9})\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{{x}^{6}}{54}-\frac{{x}^{4}}{18}]}_{0}^{3} \\  & =[\frac{27}{2}-\frac{9}{2}]-0 \\  & =9.\end{aligned}
$$
